title: do-while Loops
learningObjectives: Recognize that the body runs at least once.
Place the condition and required trailing semicolon correctly.
Trace repeated prompts and input validation.
Choose do-while for actions that must happen before testing.

understand.concept: do-while executes the body before testing the condition, guaranteeing at least one pass. It ends with a semicolon.
understand.whyItMatters: Menus and prompts often need to display once before the user chooses whether to repeat.
understand.explain: Trace body → condition → repeat or exit. Remember the trailing semicolon.

examples.title: Menu repeat
examples.code: int choice;\ndo { std::cout<<\"1 Start, 0 Exit: \"; std::cin>>choice; } while(choice!=0);
examples.explanation: The prompt occurs at least once.

examples.title: Require positive number
examples.explanation: The first input is read before the condition.

examples.title: Confirmation prompt
examples.explanation: Repeats while the user answers yes.

examples.title: One pass guaranteed
examples.explanation: The body executes once before the condition is checked.

practise.guidedTask: For do-while Loops, trace each example in a table showing the loop's initial state, condition result, body action, update step, and final state. Identify the termination point and boundary behavior.
practise.independentTask: Write a small C++ exercise focused on do-while Loops. Include at least three test cases (typical, boundary and termination/invalid-input case where relevant), trace the loop iterations, and explain why it stops or skips/continues as intended.
hints: Write down the loop's starting state.
Trace the condition before/after each pass according to loop type.
Check that every continuing path progresses toward termination.
Test boundary values and early-exit paths.
Count passes explicitly to catch off-by-one errors.

questions.explanation: The condition is checked after the body.
